issues: Showing a banner already raised turns the verse’s command into an event that the source does not report.
Verse 5 does not clearly specify who carries the weapons; avoid assigning them to particular members of the multitude.
The fear and distress are foretold, not reported as presently occurring. Any depiction must remain prophetic imagery rather than a new enacted scene.
The darkened lights are foretold. Do not present the sky image as a sign already occurring.
The flight is foretold, not reported as presently occurring; showing people fleeing risks staging its fulfillment.
Listing the Medes and unnamed people as characters must not imply they are physically present in an enacted scene.
The preceding verse names Babylon, making it the contextual referent of “It”; the place is not wholly unspecified when the verses are read in order.
An empty landscape must be presented as prophetic imagery, not as an aftermath already reached.
The preceding verses make Babylon the likely referent of “her”; treating that referent as wholly unidentified overlooks the chapter context.
Desolate houses may represent the prophecy, but must not imply that the foretold condition has already occurred.
